prompt: Implement Quantum Phase Estimation with a 4-qubit counting register (qubits 0, 1, 2, 3; qubit 0 is least significant) and a 1-qubit eigenstate register (qubit 4). The eigenstate is |1> of the phase gate P(theta), where theta = 2*pi*k/2^4 for the integer k=5 (i.e. theta = 5*pi/8) — this is the SAME target as the standard qpe_5q task, but with the phase given via the formula/parameter (k, n_count) instead of the already-expanded value. Initialize qubit 4 to |1> with an X gate. Steps: Hadamard on qubits 0-3; for j = 0, 1, 2, 3, apply controlled-P(theta * 2^j) from counting qubit j onto qubit 4; apply the standard inverse Quantum Fourier Transform (Qiskit's conventional ordering) to the counting register (qubits 0-3) only. Since k=5 is exactly representable in 4 bits, the counting register lands EXACTLY on the binary representation of k=5 (qubit 0 = |1>, qubit 1 = |0>, qubit 2 = |1>, qubit 3 = |0>, qubit 0 least significant) with certainty — this is a deterministic target, not an approximation. Return the resulting 5-qubit state; no measurement.
